title: Edmonds–Karp makes Θ(n³) reads with high probability on the max-flow entry's random dense networks
statement: Model: vertices 0..n-1, s = 0, t = n-1, M = the other m = n-2 vertices; every ordered pair is an edge independently with probability 1/2 and capacity uniform on {1..100} (generate_scaling of pairs/max-flow-edmonds-karp-vs-dinic with ideal random bits). Reads = executions of `v = to[e]` in the BFS of the entry's Edmonds-Karp code; a_v = c(s, v), b_v = c(v, t), Phi_2 = sum over M of min(a_v, b_v), D = F - c(s, t) - Phi_2, delta_M = least adjacency-list length (out- plus in-degree) of a middle vertex, mu' = E(a_v - b_v)^+ = 13433/800. Theorem 1 (deterministic, every network without parallel edges and with capacities in {1..100}): D >= 0 and reads >= delta_M D^2/20000. Theorem 2: for p1, p2 in (0, 1), y = sqrt((n-1) ln(m/p1)), x = sqrt(10^4 m ln(2/p2)/2), with probability >= 1 - p1 - p2 - B(n) (B(n) the bound on P(not C) of the trivial-min-cut note), reads >= (n-1-y)(mu' m - x)^2/20000; with p1 = p2 = 1/n, for every n >= 40, with probability >= 1 - 3/n, reads >= ell(n) n^3 whenever both factors 1 - 1/n - sqrt(2 ln n/n) and mu'(1 - 2/n) - sqrt(5000 ln(2n)/n) are positive (every n >= 98), where ell(n) = (1 - 1/n - sqrt(2 ln n/n)) (mu'(1 - 2/n) - sqrt(5000 ln(2n)/n))^2/20000; ell is non-decreasing on that range with limit mu'^2/20000 = 0.0140973...; ell(1000) >= 0.0049. Corollary 3: if D >= 200, at least floor(D/200) + 1 BFS passes each dequeue >= 1 + D/200 vertices; for n >= 40 with mu' m - x >= 200 (x for p2 = 1/n), with probability >= 1 - 3/n more than a fraction (mu' m - x)/(200(mu(n-1) + z + 1)), z = sqrt(5000(n-1) ln n), of all passes dequeue more than 1 + (mu' m - x)/200 vertices (limits 0.003325 and 0.08395625 n). Theorem 4 (every network with non-negative integer capacities): A <= F and reads <= 2E(A+1) <= 2E(F+1); on the family reads <= 2n(n-1)(100n - 99). Hence for every n >= 1000, with probability >= 1 - 3/n, 0.0049 n^3 <= Edmonds-Karp reads <= 200 n^3; with integer capacities <= 100, reads/(V E^2) <= 202/V on every network.
